cells.tense: The compass is running alongside the work right now and neither one is lagging.
cells.ask: Look at your week and name one thing you're doing that no longer feels right. Say it out loud to someone, then put it down for good, even if nobody else agrees.
cells.core:
The compass and the engine are running at the same time and neither one is dragging the other. You feel the wrong fit early — before the meeting, before the commitment. And you still have the pace to do something about it. Most people carry one of those and lose the other. You've got the timing too: what needs handing off gets handed off, what's close to done gets finished.

What is green here is taking a small, honest loss on purpose. Something you've been carrying out of habit can be set down this week, and the setting down is the point. Nothing big gets wasted — it gets weighed and released.

The balance isn't a steady state. It costs you the argument you'd like to have about it. You won't get to be right at anyone; you'll just quietly stop. That's the bill.
cells.sheetLine: You feel what's off early and you still have the pace to act.
cells.verb: Feeling what's right and carrying it into what gets done.
cells.place: The place where what you start and finish gets decided.

cells.tense: You are already bracing for the verdict on work that has not been finished yet.
cells.ask: Take one project running past its natural end and close it today with an unfinished piece showing, then leave it alone for a week and keep the week clear.
cells.core:
You're running the accounting ahead of the results. The work isn't finished yet and you've already got the ledger open — what this counts for, what it says about you, whether it comes out even. So you push. The push looks like devotion and it reads as pressure to the people in the room. Somewhere ahead you're picturing a moment where the numbers finally stand up. That moment is doing the deciding right now.

Letting somebody carry their own weight won't fix the ledger, and it isn't asked of you. Supporting someone well means holding without gripping. Let one load sit down where it is, and let them be the one who lifts it.

cells.tense: You stopped making that call back at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Say yes to one thing this week that you'd normally decline from habit, and say it before you've worked out whether you can do it.
cells.core:
The compass is there. The direction it used to give isn't. You know what feels right in the moment you feel it, and then nothing moves — it doesn't get to the hands or the calendar. Work starts and drifts. Standing still is where you live now.

What's absent isn't heart. It's a route out. Guidance, the kind that comes from a firm, gentle practice you keep — steady and plain, not harsh, just a small thing done at the same time each week, alone, so your own mind can show you the way. One small practice, kept.

Nothing has to be forced back into the bare room. Start where there's fuel and let it pull through.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's right and you've quit acting on it.
cells.verb: Feeling what's right and carrying it into what gets done.

cells.tense: The compass is giving the direction and getting no credit for it from you.
cells.ask: Pick one aim you've been treating as a requirement the world set, and say out loud to one person, 'this is mine, I chose it.' Then catch the next time you say you have to.
cells.core:
There's a version of you that keeps steering back to the right path — saying no to the thing that pays but feels wrong, staying with the work after the excitement drained out. That is the feeling of right, and it's been running the direction for a while. You talk about it like something that happened to you, or like the market decided. It didn't. This isn't a reproach. It's a fact you haven't said yet.

The simplest form of this is knowing what's what and not arguing about it. Once you say the aim is yours, you stop trying to prove it's also the correct one. It just is. That's the quiet on the far side.

Say it out loud once to someone who won't argue. Then you'll know it's yours.
cells.sheetLine: You've been steering right the whole time. Say it's you.
cells.verb: Feeling what's right and carrying it into what gets done.
cells.place: The place where what you start and finish gets decided.

attempts.check: The record's card text says 'the harvest of embodied practice expressed through feeling' and speaks of what was spilled counted against what still stands; I did not put any of that accounting vocabulary into the cells. The reader could reasonably say 'I'm not doing anything special here' — that's why the balanced cell shows the compass working through Drive as timing and boundaries rather than as a big moral moment. The ask survives a wrong read in all four because each one is a single physical act with a finish, doable today with nothing in hand, and none of them need the person to agree with the status. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'you already knew' — I cut it everywhere; it flatters the reader and shuts the person down.
